entries.text_de:
Paris, Bibl. nation., Lat. 4771, früher Colbert 3860, um 1160, vielleicht in Kent geschrieben, in Kent glossirt7, seit 15. Jh. in Frankreich.

f. 1 Cons Cnuti, u. S. 618, nur Prolog, I 1 f.

f. 1 Inst Cn, u. S. 612. 616; von I Cn 2 ab, u. S. 281, darin Theile von Af, u. S. 59 f. 71 f.; II Eg, u. S. 197 f.; auf Cn folgend Theile von Af-Ine, u. S. 63 f. 79 ff.; Mirce; Að; Had, u. S. 463 ff.; Grið, u. S. 470; Geþyncðo, u. S. 457. [Für InCn ist verwandt T.]

f. 35 Hu 8 f., u. S. 195, d. i. Cons. Cn., u. S. 619.

f. 35 Tripartita, nämlich Wl art, u. S. 486; f. 37 ECf retr, u. S. 627, und Genealogia Norman.; f. 63 Fortsetzung der Genealogia bis 1170, dann bis 11891. Cb ist copirt in Ko.
entries.text_en:
Paris, Bibliothèque nationale, Lat. 4771, formerly Colbert 3860, c. 1160, perhaps written in Kent, glossed in Kent7, in France since the 15th century.

f. 1 Cons Cnuti, below, p. 618, only the Prologue, I 1 f.

f. 1 Inst Cn, below, pp. 612. 616; from I Cn 2 onwards, below, p. 281, containing parts of Af, below, pp. 59 f. 71 f.; II Eg, below, p. 197 f.; following Cn, parts of Af-Ine, below, pp. 63 f. 79 ff.; Mirce; Að; Had, below, p. 463 ff.; Grið, below, p. 470; Geþyncðo, below, p. 457. [T is related for InCn.]

f. 35 Hu 8 f., below, p. 195, i.e. Cons. Cn., below, p. 619.

f. 35 Tripartita, namely Wl art, below, p. 486; f. 37 ECf retr, below, p. 627, and the Genealogia Norman.; f. 63 continuation of the Genealogia to 1170, then to 11891. Cb is copied in Ko.

notes.text_de: vgl. Liebermann Consil. Cnuti p. xv ff.; Transact. R. Hist. soc., N. S. VII 103.
notes.text_en: cf. Liebermann, Consil. Cnuti p. xv ff.; Transact. R. Hist. soc., N. S. VII 103.

notes.text_de: Über wapentagiis setzt Hd. 13. Jhs. id est lestis; ECf. 22, 5.
notes.text_en: Over wapentagiis a 13th-century hand writes id est lestis; ECf. 22, 5.

transcription.doubts: Roman numerals 'xv' (n. 6) and 'xvii' (n. 1, p. xxi) are printed in small capitals; given in lower case.

others.text: O’Brien (2003): dated c. 1175 rather than c. 1160. Cb is the work of a reviser: it grafts the prologue and some chapters of the Consiliatio Cnuti onto the full text, and has many readings of its own (fines spelled out in pounds and shillings, the number of oath-helpers made exact, a long added gloss at I 5,2). It shows how Cnut’s law was understood c. 1175 but is of very limited use for recovering the original text. O’Brien traces much of the trouble with Liebermann’s text to the high place he gave Cb.
